We will forever remember him. And so money is a way to acknowledge this fact. For most of human history, we used money as a symbol that cannot be paid off. But over time, as society became more sophisticated, we began using other forms of currency. Whether it's seashells, cattle, grain, women, drugs, oil—none of these work universally or store value effectively. Bronze did. After bronze, gold followed. And today, the US dollar reigns.

Bronze was a major discovery that enabled globalization. Drugs can be a form of currency, but they are not universally accepted due to societal problems like those seen with opium in China. Many governments have secret drug supplies because drugs can serve as wealth for rebuilding society if needed. Gold is also valuable but so are drugs, which people crave.

Once you have a universally accepted currency, globalization naturally follows. Capital is just the monetization of power. It exploits, alienates, and consolidates. In a village example, without money, I care about winning respect. But with capital involved, I see each person as a commodity, leading to exploitation and inequality over time.

Capitalism results in massive inequality, corruption, immorality, alienation, anger, and indifference. We have two mindsets: the altruistic nature caring for relationships and empathy versus the utilitarian side focused on material objectives and hard work. In school, the utilitarian mindset is about getting good grades; at home, it's about maintaining relationships.

Altruistic people who work for others tend to be more creative than those obsessed with money, which drives polarization as everyone rushes to make as much money as possible. Eventually, a few people have all the money, leading many to "screw this" and give up, illustrating today’s world. Capitalism changes your brain's fundamental nature.

This article from the Atlantic Monthly discusses how neuroscientists have uncovered that capitalism alters your brain, changing its basic function.
